sourceClaimAudit.correctType: fixed points of a permutation action on an exponent box
sourceClaimAudit.reason: For the Monster exponent caps [46,20,9,6,2,3,1,1,1], cap-preserving permutations have order 3!=6, not 9!. Their common fixed set has 1658160 points, not only the origin. If all nine caps were equal and positive, the full S9 action would instead fix every diagonal point.
Centrality is an invariance statement. It does not follow from, or define, decoder recovery from an action table.

sourceClaimAudit.correctType: the full irreducible-character profile separates conjugacy classes
sourceClaimAudit.reason: Characters are class functions and cannot distinguish distinct elements in the same conjugacy class. A selected family or finite head requires a separate injectivity proof.

sourceClaimAudit.correctType: a coarse invariant and a divisibility predicate
sourceClaimAudit.reason: Lagrange divisibility is necessary for element orders in a finite group but neither divisibility nor an order value normally isolates an element or class.

verdict: The source post points toward a useful reconstruction principle, but its six rows are not one theorem. The admissible common core is a typed equalizer or commuting reconstruction diagram; only after quotient, maps and equivalence are fixed can fixed points, characters, reflection and physical self-reconstruction be compared.
